name: Bamboo Soop (Winnowing Basket)
significance: Bamboo is an eco-friendly natural grass symbolizing fertility and unbroken purity. The winnowing tray separates pure grains from chaff, representing spiritual discernment. The vrati holds the sacred offerings in this tray facing the setting and rising sun.
howToUse: Cleaned thoroughly, marked with orange sindoor on the front rim. Filled with thekua, whole coconut, bananas, and autumn produce with a lit earthen diya at the center.
beginnerHack: In regions abroad where raw bamboo soop is hard to acquire, a pure brass winnowing platter (Pital ka Soop) is traditionally sanctioned and reusable.

name: Bamboo Daura (Large Basket)
significance: A deep circular bamboo basket handcrafted by village artisans. Carrying the Daura barefoot on the head to the riverbank is a supreme act of selfless surrender and seva, representing carrying the prayers of the entire household.
howToUse: Lined with a fresh yellow ritual cloth. Both morning and evening soops, thekua batches, and seasonal harvest are placed inside and carried on the head to the ghat.
beginnerHack: If travelling long distances in metro cities, carry the basket reverently on your head when departing home and arriving onto the riverbank.

name: Mitti Ka Hathi (Terracotta Elephant)
significance: Handcrafted terracotta clay elephant decorated with sacred vermilion and turmeric motifs. It bears an earthen diya on its back and forms the sacred heart of the night-long Kosi Bharai vigil to fulfill family vows (Mannat).
howToUse: Placed at the center beneath a 5-sugarcane canopy (Chhatri) surrounded by 24 clay lamps, filled with offerings and kept glowing with sesame or mustard oil through the night.
beginnerHack: Terracotta artisans in Purvanchal and Bihar craft these for Chhath; in metro diaspora communities, a clean terracotta or brass elephant figurine is lovingly used.

name: Brass / Copper Lota, Kalash & Thali
hindi: तांबे-पीतल का लोटा, कलश और थाली
significance: Copper and brass are solar metals in Vedic tradition. Offering holy water and raw cow milk through a copper pitcher balances the bio-energetic stream and catches the first rays of the dawn sun.
howToUse: Filled with pure Gangajal, fresh water, raw cow milk, red flowers, and akshat. Poured in a slow continuous stream over the edge of the bamboo soop into the river.
beginnerHack: Any dedicated clean brass (pital) or copper tumbler can be purified with Gangajal and used for offering Arghya.

name: Whole Sugarcane with Leaves (5–7 Stalks)
significance: Tall sugarcane stalks with their lush green leaves intact symbolize the sweetness of nature and agrarian abundance. Tied at the top, they create the iconic pyramidal canopy (Kosi Chhatri).
howToUse: Five to seven stalks are tied at the apex with sacred red thread to form a tent over the earthen elephant and prasad on the riverbank.
beginnerHack: In apartment balconies or overseas, 5 clean sugarcane stalks tied in a quiet corner create the authentic spiritual Kosi altar.

name: Whole Coconut with Water & Banana Bunch
hindi: पानी वाला नारियल और केले का घौद
bhojpuri: जटा नारियल आ केरा के घौद
significance: The whole fibrous coconut represents the human ego offered with its water to the cosmos. An entire bunch of bananas, apples, oranges, guavas, pears, and custard apples (Sharifa) honor the autumn harvest.
howToUse: Placed prominently at the center of the bamboo soop next to the lit diya before stepping into the river.
beginnerHack: Any seasonal, chemical-free local fruits available in your city (sweet limes, pears, pomegranates) are deeply welcomed by Surya Dev.

name: Dabh Nimbu, Singhara & Shakarkandi
significance: Dabh Nimbu (giant thick-skinned wild pomelo) represents seasonal immunity. Water chestnuts (Singhara), sweet potatoes (Shakarkandi), radishes with leaves (Mooli), and Suthni tubers celebrate sacred earth roots.
howToUse: Arranged symmetrically inside the bamboo soop. Root vegetables are cleaned thoroughly and kept whole with green tops intact.
beginnerHack: Look for pomelo / grapefruit in Asian or farmers' markets; they are the exact botanical family of Chhath's sacred Dabh Nimbu.

name: Pila Sindoor, Akshat & Kumkum
hindi: पीला मटिया सिन्दूर, अक्षत और चन्दन
significance: Traditional Chhath sindoor is natural bright saffron-orange (Matiya Sindoor), symbolizing the blazing solar path. Akshat (unbroken sun-dried rice mixed with turmeric) represents wholeness and unblemished devotion.
howToUse: Applied to the bamboo soop, daura, and clay elephant. Vratis apply a long line from the bridge of the nose upwards, and share with fellow devotees on the riverbank.
beginnerHack: Ensure you buy lead-free organic herbal orange sindoor, commonly labeled as 'Bihari Chhath Matiya Sindoor'.

name: Paan, Supari, Gangajal, Kapur & Dhoop
hindi: पान, सुपारी, गंगाजल, कपूर और धूप
significance: Fresh betel leaves (Paan) and whole areca nuts (Supari) symbolize respect and hospitality for nature deities. Sacred Gangajal purifies the vessels, while Kapur (camphor) and aromatic dhoop cleanse the morning air.
howToUse: Placed on the soop with flowers, sacred Kalava thread, honey (Shahad), and fresh green Durva grass before performing the solar aarti.
beginnerHack: A single copper lota with a few drops of Gangajal mixed with fresh water sanctifies the entire ritual space anywhere in the world.

name: Thekua Mahaprasad (Atta, Gur & Ghee)
significance: The timeless signature prasad of Chhath Mahaparv. Prepared with stone-ground whole wheat flour (Atta), organic sugarcane jaggery (Gur), pure desi cow ghee, and aromatic fennel seeds (Saunf).
howToUse: Moulded on wooden saanchas with sun-burst and leaf carvings, deep-fried in pure ghee in a sanctified kitchen on Day 3, and loaded into every Arghya soop.
beginnerHack: If you lack a traditional wooden mould, gently press the dough balls with the back of a fork or strainer for classic festive ridges.

name: Kasar Laddus & Kharna Kheer (Rasiya)
hindi: कसार के लड्डू और खरना की खीर
significance: Kasar laddus are handcrafted from roasted rice flour, crushed jaggery, and cow ghee. Kharna Kheer (Rasiya) is sacred rice pudding slow-cooked in pure milk and jaggery on Day 2 to inaugurate the 36-hour nirjala fast.
howToUse: Offered in fresh earthen or brass bowls on banana leaves in absolute silence at sunset, followed by whole wheat rotis.
beginnerHack: Use organic non-iodized jaggery and full-fat cow milk to achieve the rich golden caramel flavor of authentic Bihari Rasiya.

name: Mitti Ka Chulha, Lauki Meal & Peele Vastra
hindi: मिट्टी का चूल्हा, कद्दू-भात और पीले वस्त्र
significance: The virgin clay stove fueled with dry mango wood represents elemental purity. Day 1 Nahay-Khay meal consists of tender bottle gourd (Lauki), Chana dal, and Arwa rice cooked in Sendha Namak (rock salt). Devotees wear fresh unstitched yellow/saffron cotton clothes (Peele Vastra).
howToUse: The entire meal is cooked in virgin vessels without onion or garlic. Eaten by the vrati first, purifying body and mind before the fast.
beginnerHack: Where wood fire is restricted by apartment codes, an electric induction cooker or virgin stove dedicated exclusively to puja fulfills the vow.
